name: mix60sft_s2_long_q8_s20261026
description: mix60 list with SFT traces: long context
validation: 300 single-turn prompts shared by every list (ranks val_ranks)
columns: mix_domain (reasoning / code / bfcl / tau2 / long / val), mix_part (main / buffer), mix_src_rank (rank in its source list), response (the written SFT trace as Qwen3's chat template writes the assistant turn after the rendered prompt, or null: the student generates the row), len_response (its Qwen3 tokens)
rule: SFT-trace version of the mix60 Qwen3-8B list. Each row has the written assistant reply of its source dataset (an SFT trace) where one exists for exactly the row's prompt and fits the window (prompt + response <= 131,072): replies without reasoning, calls of functions the tool list lacks and Chinese replies kept as written; for math the trace of the row's effort level without python, else another level's; otherwise one chosen at random (seed 20261023). A row without a usable trace (no trace, only tool-using traces, cut-off or empty replies, over the window, written for another prompt form) has no response and is generated by the student in the same run. Multi-turn conversations with a trace (customer service and function calling in the customer-service portion) are one sample per conversation: the recorded final answer as the response and every earlier assistant answer supervised (hist_sup). SFT-SWE-v2 rows keep the list's prompt, which drops the formatting paragraph of the dataset's prompt as in every arm; its replies were written for the prompt with that paragraph, so a reply that uses that formatting is not used and the others are. Sizes: each domain is cut where it holds the same packed-token target as the mix60 list (60 steps of data), counting a traced row as prompt + response and a generated row as the mix60 list estimates it (its own prompt plus the mean generated length measured for its kind of row; customer-service conversations: the measured packed tokens per conversation), continuing the domain's own row sequence where the traces are shorter than the student's answers; then a 10 % buffer of the next rows (code and function calling, whose mix60 lists hold more than the target: cut along the mix60 order, the rows after the cut as the buffer, at most 10 %: code 10 %, function calling 9 %). Domains interleaved as in mix60.
